blocks.text: JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Jephthah. Chosen head of Gilead; broke Ammon; judged Israel six years.
LED ISRAELi
6 years No years BC in Scripture
TRIBE
Not stated (a Gileadite)
IN THE LINE
9th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah.”
PROPHETS
None named
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD Israel served Baalim, Ashtaroth and the gods of Syria, Zidon, Moab, Ammon and the Philistines. Judges 10:6

2 · OPPRESSED: THE AMMONITES (WITH THE PHILISTINES), 18 YEARS The LORD sold Israel to the Philistines and the Ammonites; for eighteen years the Ammonites oppressed Israel in Gilead, and crossed the Jordan to fight Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim. Judges 10:7–9
3 · CRIED OUT Israel cried "We have sinned"; the LORD answered "I will deliver you no more"; they put away the strange gods, and "his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel". Judges 10:10–16
4 · DELIVERED Jephthah struck Ammon "from Aroer, even till thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities". Judges 11:32–33
5 · REST Scripture does not say.
ACCESSION
How Jephthah came to power
His half-brothers drove him out; he lived in the land of Tob, where "vain men" gathered to him. Judges 11:2–3
When Ammon made war, the elders of Gilead came to fetch him as captain. Judges 11:4–8
He asked, "shall I be your head?"; the people made him "head and captain over them", and he spoke all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh. Judges 11:9–11
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah." Judges 11:29
He laid Israel's case before the king of Ammon: "the LORD the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon". Judges 11:27
Samuel names him among the deliverers; Hebrews among those who acted by faith. 1 Samuel 12:11 Hebrews 11:32

THE NATION
What the nation did
Israel put away the strange gods "and served the LORD". Judges 10:16
"It was a custom in Israel" for the daughters of Israel to lament Jephthah's daughter four days a year. Judges 11:39–40
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
AMMON

THE PHILISTINES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Eighteen years of Ammonite oppression and six years of judging (Judges 10:8, 12:7). Jephthah's "three hundred years" (11:26) is Scripture's own long count; see the open question.
No, she was given to the LORD in lifelong virginity
First found in the Kimchis (late 12th century), as reported by Moore; Keil (1865)

Keil reads "she knew no man" as the way the vow was fulfilled, a "spiritual burnt-offering, in a lifelong chastity", and argues that the writer would not have described a human sacrifice without blame.[5][27]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage

PASSAGES · 3
Judges 10:6–12:7 1 Samuel 12:11 Hebrews 11:32
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Jephthah's daughter, and gives no verdict on the vow.
No prophet is named in Jephthah's story; the LORD's answer to Israel's cry in Judges 10:11-14 is given without a messenger's name.
Judges does not say Jephthah judged all Israel; the war and his election belong to Gilead (Judges 10:17-11:11).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
"Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah." Judges 11:1
